title: Pressure
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Press a finger and a pencil point into clay or soft soap with the same push; stand a bottle with three holes at different heights full of water outdoors; compare a sharp and a blunt knife on a tomato. The child predicts before each test.

skills.key_step: The child says pressure grows with a bigger force or a smaller area (pressure = force / area), liquid pressure grows with depth, and uses this to explain applications (sharp knives, wide tyres and camel feet, dam walls thicker at the bottom).

floor.prerequisite: Can find the area of a rectangle.
floor.question: What is the area of a 2 m by 3 m floor?

representations: finger and pencil pressed into clay
a bottle with holes at three heights
a chart: application, more or less pressure, why
steps: Same force, smaller area: more pressure (a pencil point).
Same force, larger area: less pressure (wide tyres).
Liquid pressure grows with depth (lowest hole squirts furthest).
Use pressure = force / area for a simple sum.
contexts: a lorry with wide tyres on a muddy road

board.do: Draw a bottle with three holes at different heights.
Ask which hole will squirt furthest.
Draw the bottom jet longest and write "pressure grows with depth".

misconceptions.ask: Same push: why did the pencil sink deeper than the finger?
misconceptions.repair: A smaller area gives a bigger pressure.

listen_for: a larger area gives more pressure
misconceptions.ask: Why do wide tyres not sink in mud?
misconceptions.repair: A larger area spreads the force.

listen_for: pressure is the same at all depths
the wide tank has more pressure
misconceptions.ask: Did the jets from the wide and narrow bottles go the same distance?

checks.question: Why is a dam wall thicker at the bottom?
checks.answer: water pressure is greatest at the bottom (it grows with depth)

checks.question: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one?
checks.answer: the same force acts on a smaller area, giving more pressure
